# Savewave

## Overview

Savewave uses the flow Paste -> Resolve -> Preview -> Save inside its native applications. The Vercel deployment is a lightweight installation landing page only. Public-media extraction belongs to native builds and runs locally through yt-dlp and FFmpeg.

## Architecture

- Shared TypeScript core: source detection, capabilities, normalized errors and progress, filenames, quality policy, Spotify scoring, and bounded IndexedDB history.
- Website: installation and product information only, with no downloader or cloud extraction fallback.
- Desktop adapter: Tauri commands backed by Rust-managed local sidecars, isolated temporary files, progress and cancellation.
- Android source: Kotlin/youtubedl-android MediaStore work in progress; no APK is advertised until device validation is complete.
- No iOS target, remote extraction VPS, browser cookies, or session import.

Supported Windows sources include publicly resolvable YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, X/Twitter, SoundCloud and direct media. Private, login-gated, cookie-only, paid and DRM-protected content is unsupported. Spotify audio is never downloaded from Spotify; Smart Match uses public metadata and rejects ambiguous candidates.

The installed Windows client checks the website's small version manifest at launch. A newer version produces an update notice with explicit installer and changelog links; Savewave does not silently replace executables.

## Privacy and security

- No accounts or application database.
- No cloud media extraction, proxying, upload or permanent storage.
- Native inputs are limited to public HTTP(S) targets and sidecars use structured arguments.
- Download history stays inside the installed application on that device and can be cleared.
- Source platforms still receive the user's network request; absolute anonymity is not claimed.

Only download media you own or are authorized to save, subject to source terms and applicable law.
